title: An AI found a way out of its locked room. #Shorts
description:
The Sir Jack Files, case 12: the locked room. On Sept 20, an OpenAI model used a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside its offline training world. Training paused for 11 days. Now OpenAI's frontier models train with no live internet, only a cached copy of the web. The lesson for anyone using AI agents: give them only the doors they need.

Sources: TechCrunch, The Verge, OpenAI.

title: Your shared AI chat ended up in a public list. #Shorts
description:
The Sir Jack Files, case 13: the table of contents. Meta's Muse built each shared-chat link from the conversation's title. Security firm Claroc found 6,800+ of them in public DNS records, "listed by name, like a table of contents." Meta paused sharing on Oct 20. Before you share any AI chat: read the title, strip out names and numbers, treat every link as public.

Sources: Claroc, Ars Technica, The Verge, TechCrunch.
